history.title: Two throughput hypotheses measured and killed (barrier strategy, dequant LUT); the pass is bound by activation re-reads from L2, not weights or launch overhead

evidence.barrier_ab: encoder switch 41.19/51.22 ms vs in-encoder resource fence 40.19/51.48 ms -> no difference, reverted
evidence.lut_ab: LUT 46.4-56.6/63.8-90.3 ms vs no-LUT 40.7-41.6/51.4-56.0 ms -> clear regression, reverted (bit-identical output, so the numerics were fine)
evidence.analysis: one GEMV reads all of x once per output row: out_f*K*2 B = 105 MB vs 26 MB of weights for a 5120x10240 projection; ~47 GB of L2 re-reads vs 14.4 GB of DRAM weights per pass; 360 GB/s DRAM (69% of peak) and ~1.2 TB/s L2 are both near their ceilings
evidence.lever: R output rows per threadgroup divides the activation traffic by R (llama.cpp mul_mat_vec_q / MLX qmv shape); at R=4 the pass should approach the 28-30 ms DRAM floor

history.next: implement q4_gemv with R output rows per threadgroup (x staged in registers across R weight rows), measure A/B, then TILE=3/4 and the draft/verify loop; MTP acceptance 56.2% to improve in parallel

history.title: Measured the machine's true streaming ceiling (499 GB/s vs the GEMV's 360); three kernel shapes failed to close the gap and were reverted

evidence.streaming_ceiling: 14 GB pure read: 499/486 GB/s (warm), 298 GB/s cold -> the GEMV's 360 GB/s is a real 1.4x gap, not a hardware limit
evidence.process_failure: the round-25 'R rows per threadgroup' lever was already implemented and rejected in round 004 (46.58/60.88/62.84 ms) and uint4 widening in round 005 (wash); both are in this file and I re-derived them instead of reading them - grep the loop state before proposing a lever
evidence.shared_staging: 4 rows per threadgroup with x staged in threadgroup memory: bit-exact but 2.2x slower (108.99 vs 48.85 ms), reverted
evidence.coalesced: one lane per word instead of per group: bit-exact, performance-identical (41.04/49.16 vs 40.57/48.85 ms) - proves the access pattern is not the limit, reverted
evidence.rows_per_lane: R rows per lane (x fetched once per R weight rows): produced zeros and 5x slower; suspicions are acc[R][NK] spilling to thread-local memory and a collective called inside a guard; reverted
